Title: Tenant VPC Activation Playbook — Handoff Checklist + Terraform Safeguards
Body:
Purpose

Quick, pragmatic activation playbook for tenant VPCs. Targets customer-facing Private deployments (VPC and on-prem) where we own the control plane but customer owns networking. This is a working checklist for Solutions Eng + Private Deployments SRE to complete an activation with minimal back-and-forth.

Scope
- Customer-provisioned VPCs (cloud: AWS/GCP), single-tenant, multi-AZ preferred.
- Applies to both greenfield and brownfield (migration) activations.
- Includes Terraform module hardening notes, state/backend considerations, and upgrade/rollback steps for module changes.

Non-goals
- Deep-dive into customer firewall configuration (we provide suggested rules only)
- On-prem physical cabling and rack level implementation details

High-level flow (one-liner)
1) Pre-kickoff (docs + prep) -> 2) Kickoff + network validation -> 3) TF plan & staging apply -> 4) App onboarding + smoke tests -> 5) Cutover -> 6) Post-activation review

Pre-kickoff (deliverables we prepare)
- Tenant activation questionnaire (CIDR, AZs, NAT/egress preference, allowed outbound CIDRs, KMS policy, peering/transit expectations)
- Customer VPC template: minimal subnets (control/data), route tables, IGW/NAT choices, private endpoints list
- TF module version pinning recommendations for the customer's lifecycle
- Confluence page for the activation with links to tickets, runbook, and contact points

Kickoff checklist (30–45m call)
- Confirm CIDR plan and AZs (no overlapping CIDR with central infra)
- Discuss egress model (NAT gateway per AZ, central egress via Transit Gateway, or private egress via proxy)
- Confirm GSIs: KMS Key ARNs (or customer will grant), Customer's Cloud IAM roles for control-plane hookups
- Agree on maintenance window for config changes and potential service restarts
- Identify networking owners and emergency contact (pager/Slack)

Network reference architecture notes (practical recommendations)
- Subnet model: 3 AZs, for each AZ: control-subnet (private, route to TGW/VPN), workload-subnet (private, auto-scaling), public-subnet limited to bastion/NAT if required.
- Routing: prefer Transit Gateway for multi-account setups; otherwise use VPC Peering with explicit routes. Avoid transitive routing with peering.
- Egress: prefer NAT gateway per AZ for low-latency egress; for cost-sensitive customers, central egress with autoscaling NAT instances is acceptable but increases blast radius.
- Private endpoints: require endpoints for S3/GCS, ECR/GCR, and control-plane telemetry. Document expected prefixes and ensure customer egress policies allow them.
- Security groups vs. NACLs: favor SGs for app-level controls, NACLs for edge rate-limits. Keep SGs narrow (IP ranges + ports) and tag consistently.
- BGP/MPLS (onprem): when SRv6 or BGP is in place, expect longer churn; allocate 2–4 hours for BGP adj/route convergence validation during cutover.

Terraform module notes (practical guardrails)
- Pin module versions: modules should be pinned in tenant manifests (module source ref + semver). Example: module "vpc" { source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//vpc?ref=v1.8.2" }
- State backend: require remote state backend (S3/GCS) with kms encryption and state locking (DynamoDB for S3). Customer-managed or Redwood-managed backend to be agreed in kickoff.
- Workspaces: use per-tenant workspace or per-environment workspace to reduce accidental cross-tenant drift.
- Plan reviews: all terraform apply must be preceded by an RFC in the activation ticket with the TF plan attached. No blind applies.
- Immutable resource handling: for resources that require replacement (e.g., changing central CIDR), provide migration modules to create parallel resources and cut traffic.
- Idempotency: modules must be idempotent — add guard checks in modules to avoid recreating default route tables or altering shared resources unintentionally.
- Outputs and tagging: every module must export resource ids (vpc_id, subnet_ids, route_table_ids). Enforce tagging policy: project=redwood, tenant=<tenant-id>, env=<env>.

Helpful TF snippet (sample module pin + backend)

// backend.tf (recommendation)
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket = "rdw-tf-state-tenant-{{tenant_id}}"
    key    = "vpc/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "us-west-2"
    encrypt = true
    kms_key_id = "arn:aws:kms:..."
  }
}

module "vpc" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//vpc?ref=v1.8.2"
  tenant_id = var.tenant_id
  cidr_block = var.cidr_block
  azs = var.azs
}

Staging and pre-flight (CI)
- CI step must run: terraform init && terraform validate && terraform plan -out=plan.out
- Plan must be uploaded to the activation ticket and acked by SRE and Solutions Eng before apply.
- Smoke deploy into staging VPC first (or a shadow tenant) and run these quick checks:
  - Control plane connectivity: can control plane reach private endpoints over expected ports?
  - KV cache path validation: ensure egress to model object store or registry is allowed.
  - Latency sanity: pings to NAT/proxy, traceroutes recorded.

Upgrade plan for TF modules and runtime images
- Strategy: conservative small-batch upgrades using canaries (1 tenant at a time for major changes, 5–10% of tenants for moderate changes)
- Versioning rules:
  - Patch: opt-in, schedule allowed within maintenance windows
  - Minor: run CI, smoke, and one canary tenant before broad rollout
  - Major: require design doc, migration plan, and DB/IPC compatibility checks (if any)
- Module changes that touch shared infra (Transit Gateway, central NAT) require cross-team signoff (infra, sre, security)
- Rolling upgrade steps:
  1) Create parallel resources if change is disruptive (new subnets, new TGW attachments)
  2) Update TF ref and plan against staging tenant
  3) Apply to canary tenant, validate, monitor metrics for 24–48 hrs
  4) Broad rollout in waves with monitoring and quick rollback playbook

Rollback playbook (fast revert)
- If apply causes regressions (network partitions, failure to reach object stores, broken healthchecks):
  - Pause rollout (automated gate via runbook)
  - Apply previous TF state snapshot: terraform apply using last-known-good plan (we keep plan artifacts in S3 archive)
  - For stateful destructive changes, run compensating scripts from archived runbooks
  - Notify customer and open incident with severity level mapped to SLA

Cutover checklist (execution window)
- Pre-window: run final terraform plan and snapshot state
- Bring engineers online (SRE, Solutions Eng, customer L2)
- Drain traffic if necessary (for migrations)
- Apply TF with a single person responsible for apply and a second person watching logs
- Validate connectivity, healthchecks, and model-serving endpoints
- Post-window: run full acceptance tests and tag activation ticket with verification artifacts

Observability and SLOs during activation
- Enable high-fidelity logs for the activation window (retain extra for 72 hrs)
- Monitor these signals:
  - Control-plane API latency
  - Failed connections to model storage/registry
  - Error rates on auth/token exchange
- If errors spike > 3x baseline for 15 minutes, trigger rollback

Operational tips and gotchas (notes from field)
- Customers sometimes use overly broad CIDR ranges; insist on at most /16 for tenant VPCs to avoid AWS route table size traps.
- Shared ECR/GCR egress often blocked; confirm registry IP ranges early.
- Terraform provider drift: pinned provider versions are as important as module pins. Test provider upgrades in staging.
- NAT cost surprises: estimate per-AZ NAT data transfer and present cost comparison for per-AZ vs centralized egress.
- Onprem BGP: expect MTU/fragmentation issues if tunnels are not negotiated with jumbo frames; verify with iperf.

Open questions (to resolve per-customer)
- Who will manage remote state? Customer or Redwood? (default: customer-managed for compliance customers)
- Encryption: customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed key
- Backup retention window for TF state and plan artifacts

Post-activation responsibilities
- 7-day check-in: confirm metrics stable and no recurring errors
- 30-day retrospective: collect lessons, add to module docs if recurring friction seen
- Tag all deployed resources with activation ticket ID and tenant tag for billing/tracing

Appendix: quick checklist for field engineer (copyable)
- [ ] Confirm CIDR and AZs
- [ ] Confirm KMS & IAM roles
- [ ] Confirm remote state backend details
- [ ] Run terraform init/plan in staging
- [ ] Upload plan to ticket and get ack
- [ ] Apply in staging and run smoke tests
- [ ] Schedule cutover window and notify customer
- [ ] Apply in prod (one responsible engineer)
- [ ] Validate healthchecks, connectivity
- [ ] Post-activation runbook and tag resources
